runningHomeComparison.purpose: Real-browser placement/context diagnostic only; candidate is not wired into these captures.

contractUsed: Avatar-safe corridor approximately x=36-64% and y=18-88%.
Dominant architectural hotspot must stay out of that corridor.
Preserve bed-left / desk-right anchors and clean center floor for separate character composition.

observations: The v2 repair clearly fixes the v1 hotspot problem: the strongest window/daylight source is confined to the far-left side, while the upper central wall is comparatively calm and gives UI/character layers useful contrast.

The rendered pixels have materially stronger depth cues than the current running Home background: rounded furniture volumes, floor contact, textile response, bevel highlights, shelf depth and directional warm light all read cleanly without baked UI.

The lower avatar corridor is not actually clean enough for integration. The bed/footboard extends from the left into roughly the middle of the x=36-64% contract corridor, while the plant/chair intrude from the right edge of that same corridor. The remaining lower-center gap is too narrow for the large separate avatar presentation visible in the real Home browser capture.

A deterministic center-cover diagnostic of the exact 1408x1056 asset at 390x844 corresponds to an uncropped-source window of approximately x=460-948 across the full source height. That slice retains the bed edge on the left and plant/chair on the right, putting competing silhouettes directly behind the likely phone hero area. At 320x568 the center-cover source window is approximately x=407-1001 and has the same conflict. These are diagnostic crops, not claims about the final runtime CSS.

The 1408x1056 derivative is a reasonable desktop/tablet candidate payload at 1,394,961 bytes for preproduction evaluation. The 3,808,983-byte full source should not be the default phone runtime asset; a purpose-built phone derivative/crop would improve both composition and transfer cost. No measured network/FPS claim is made.

Provide a phone-oriented derivative or documented art-direction crop rather than relying on center-cover of the 4:3 desktop asset.
